findings.title: Any Combat-type card played as a defense — including pure attack cards and unparsed text — resolves as a full stop
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:298 "The card you are defending with must defend against the type of attack your opponent is performing." CRD:301-308 lists the five legal ways to defend, all of which require a card/effect that actually stops the attack or prevents its damage. CRD:340 "8) If the attack is not stopped at this time, the attack is considered successful." CRD:742 "Some cards can perform AND stop attacks. Such cards can only be played as either an attack or to stop an attack."
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:597-613 (the `stops.length === 0` fallback sets `atk.stopped = true`); packages/engine/src/combat.ts:862-869 (`defenseEffects` falls back to ALL of a card's abilities when none has trigger 'defense'); packages/engine/src/combat.ts:872-874 (`defenseStops` filters for stopAttack only); packages/engine/src/combat.ts:444-461 (`combatCardError` gates only on card TYPE)
findings.defect: resolveDefense validates only that the card is the defender's, is in hand or in play, and is typed Physical Combat / Energy Combat / Combat. It then asks `defenseStops` what the card stops. `defenseEffects` filters for abilities with trigger 'defense' and, finding none, returns the card's ATTACK ability effects instead (combat.ts:868-869). Those contain no `stopAttack`, so `stops.length === 0` and control falls to the else branch at line 609, which logs "Defense card has no modelled stop — resolving it as a stop; verify by hand." and then unconditionally sets `atk.stopped = true` at line 613. The type-matching check at lines 602-608 is skipped entirely on that path, and nothing distinguishes "unparsed text" from "parsed, and it is an attack". The card's remaining effects are then applied as defensive riders via applyOnPlay (line 625-630), so an attack card's stage-drain/anger effects also fire against the attacker.
findings.consequence: Every Physical/Energy Combat card in hand doubles as a universal block against either attack type — 30 such attack-only cards exist in data/cards.saiyan.enriched.json alone (Standing Fist Punch, One Knuckle Punch, Lunge Punch). A defender never has to hold real defense cards, an energy-only block's type restriction is bypassed by using an attack-only card instead, and combat degenerates into "whoever runs out of cards last": no attack lands while the defender holds anything.
findings.verifiedBy: combat.ts:862-870 `const defensive = abilities.filter((a) => a.trigger === 'defense'); return (defensive.length > 0 ? defensive : abilities).flatMap((a) => a.effects);` — an attack-only card contributes its attack effects. combat.ts:598 `if (stops.length > 0) {` guards the type-match block at 602-608 (`const covers = nowStops.some(...)`); the else at 609-611 only logs 'Defense card has no modelled stop — resolving it as a stop; verify by hand.' and execution reaches combat.ts:613 `atk.stopped = true;` unconditionally, skipping the covers check. combatCardError (combat.ts:444-461) gates only on `COMBAT_CARD_TYPES.has(type)` and returns undefined for 'Unknown' and for any in-play card. Riders then fire via applyOnPlay at combat.ts:625-630. RUNTIME CONFIRMATION against the built engine: a card whose text is "Physical attack doing 3 power stages of damage" was accepted as the defense to an ENERGY attack and stopped it (log: "Effect not yet automated: physicalAttack (resolve manually)." then "P1 stops the attack."). Data count: 30 cards in data/cards.saiyan.enriched.json are typed Physical/Energy Combat with a parsed attack effect and no stopAttack. No test in packages/engine/src/*.test.ts touches the 'no modelled stop' path. CRD:298, CRD:301-308 and CRD:742 read as quoted.

findings.title: A defense card used from play is never spent, so one permanent blocks every attack forever
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:306-307 lists using a Non-Combat card in play as a way to defend; CRD:2519 "Defense Shields attempt to stop the FIRST unstopped attack"; CRD:1566 Fall 7 Times — "Remove from the game after use."
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:477-484 (spend() inside discardAttackCards), called from combat.ts:632
findings.defect: discardAttackCards' spend() looks the card up with p.zones.hand.findIndex and returns immediately when the index is -1, so a card defended with from zones.inPlay is never moved, never removed from the game, and — unlike the step-7 shield path, which records c.shieldsUsed at combat.ts:392/403 — is never recorded as used. resolveDefense (combat.ts:589-637) has no per-combat or per-turn usage check of its own.
findings.consequence: Any player holding one defensive Drill, Mastery, or Defense Shield in play is immune to attacks for the rest of the game — they simply name the same permanent as their defense in every Attack Phase. "Remove from the game after use" is silently ignored on this path.
findings.verifiedBy: discardAttackCards' spend() at combat.ts:481-483 reads `const at = p.zones.hand.findIndex((c) => c.uid === uid); if (at === -1) return;`, so the removeFromGameAfterUse branch at combat.ts:498-502 is unreachable for a card in inPlay, and resolveDefense (combat.ts:589-637) records nothing comparable to the step-7 shield path's `c.shieldsUsed = [...(c.shieldsUsed ?? []), inst.uid]` (combat.ts:403). Runtime: Orange Hiding Drill in play stopped three consecutive energy attacks in one combat with the life deck unchanged (30-3=27 throughout) and the card still in inPlay; Fall 7 Times ('Remove from the game after use.', CRD:1566) parsed with a removeFromGameAfterUse effect yet finished with inPlay=1, removed=0. combat-reentry.test.ts 'a card that defended from play stays in play' only asserts the permanent is not discarded — nothing about repeat use or removal-after-use.

findings.title: The Discard Step does nothing — the 1-card hand limit is never enforced
findings.crdEvidence: CRD.txt L240-241: "6) Discard Step: If you are the attacker and you have more than 1 card in your hand during this step, place all but 1 of your cards into the discard pile... you may have no more than 1 card in your hand at the end of this step. Your opponent does the same, right after you discard."
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:80-95 (advanceStep case handles only 'draw', 'powerUp', 'combat'); packages/engine/src/turn.ts:45-66 (advanceStep only moves the step pointer)
findings.defect: 'discard' is a step name in STEPS (packages/shared/src/state.ts:6-14) with no behaviour attached. The reducer's advanceStep branch fires draw() on entering 'draw', powerUp() on entering 'powerUp' and beginCombat() on entering 'combat', and nothing at all on entering 'discard' or 'rejuvenation'. A repo-wide grep for a hand cap (hand.length limit / MAX_HAND / HAND_LIMIT) finds no enforcement anywhere in engine, server or client — the only hand.splice is abilities.ts:168 for a card effect. Neither player ever discards down to 1.
findings.consequence: Hands grow without bound. The attacker gains 3 cards every Draw Step (turn.ts:22 DRAW_PER_TURN) and the defender gains 3 more every Prepare Phase (combat.ts:79), and none of it is ever trimmed, so by turn 5 each player is holding a dozen-plus cards. The game's central resource constraint — you end every turn with one card — is absent, which changes every play decision: cards are hoarded for the perfect turn instead of being spent or lost, defense is always available, and Life Decks empty far faster than the Survival race is balanced for.
findings.verifiedBy: CRD.txt L240-241 reads verbatim as quoted: "you may have no more than 1 card in your hand at the end of this step. Your opponent does the same, right after you discard." In packages/engine/src/reducer.ts the entire advanceStep case is lines 80-95, and its only post-advance work is `if (state.step === 'draw') draw(...); else if (state.step === 'powerUp') powerUp(...); else if (state.step === 'combat') beginCombat(...)` (reducer.ts:91-93) — no 'discard' branch. packages/engine/src/turn.ts:46-67 advanceStep only sets state.step, pushes a stepChanged event and a log line; the sole special case is the skipCombatThisTurn redirect at turn.ts:58-63. Repo-wide grep for hand.length/MAX_HAND/HAND_LIMIT across packages/ returns only client display code (Board.tsx:45, 179), test assertions, and abilities.ts:168 `p.zones.hand.splice(0, Math.min(count, p.zones.hand.length))` inside discardFromHand (a card effect). No test in packages/engine/src/*.test.ts asserts a hand cap.

findings.title: An attack can be declared with no card, no personality power and no cost, unlimited times per Attack Phase sequence
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:283-291 enumerates the seven things you may do in an Attack Phase: play a card that can perform an attack from hand, use a card in play that can perform an attack, use a Non-Combat card, play a card and discard it, use a Personality power, perform a Final Physical Attack, or pass. CRD:374 "Personalities can only attack if they are in control of Combat" (a power still has to exist and be paid for).
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:213-233 (`cardUid: string | undefined`; the card check at line 230 is `if (cardUid)`, so a bare declaration skips all validation); packages/client/src/components/Board.tsx:194-195 (`onAttack('physical')` / `onAttack('energy')` buttons send no cardUid)
findings.defect: declareAttack accepts an attack with no cardUid and no ability. Nothing is spent: `discardAttackCards` (line 477-484) returns immediately when `uid` is undefined, so no hand card leaves the hand. There is no check that the acting player has any card or power capable of performing the attack. The client exposes this as two plain buttons in the combat panel.
findings.consequence: On every Attack Phase a player can press "Physical attack" and deal full PAT power-stage damage without playing or discarding anything, forever, while keeping their whole hand for defense. Hand management, deck construction and card economy — the resources the CRD's Attack Phase options are built around — stop mattering; a player with an empty hand attacks exactly as effectively as one with a full hand.
findings.verifiedBy: combat.ts:213-233: the signature takes `cardUid: string | undefined` and the only validation is combat.ts:230 `if (cardUid) { const bad = combatCardError(...) }` — with no cardUid every card/power check is skipped, and the reducer at reducer.ts:157-163 likewise only looks up an ability `if (action.cardUid)`. Nothing is spent: discardAttackCards' `spend` helper begins `if (!uid) return;` (combat.ts:478-479). Board.tsx:194-195 are verbatim `<button onClick={() => onAttack('physical')}>Physical attack</button>` / `onAttack('energy')`, sending no cardUid. CRD:283-291 enumerates the seven Attack Phase options as quoted, none of which is a bare cardless, costless attack.

findings.title: Powering up is repeatable: the auto power-up fires and a manual powerUp action can then repeat it without limit
findings.crdEvidence: CRD.txt L228-229: "3) Power-Up Step — If you are the attacker, yout Main Personality powers up by moving his Scouter up a number of power stages equal to his Power Up Rating (PUR)." CRD.txt L2551: "Powering Up: This occurs during the Power Up Step of the Sequence of Play." — one power-up, in that step.
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:92 (auto) and packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:99-101 (manual, unguarded)
findings.defect: Entering the Power-Up Step already applies the full power-up: reducer.ts:92 `else if (state.step === 'powerUp') powerUp(state, state.activePlayerIdx, db, events)`. The separate `powerUp` action at reducer.ts:99-101 calls the same turn.ts:130 powerUp() with no check of state.step, no check that the actor is the active player, and no once-per-turn flag anywhere in GameState. The server's authorize() (packages/server/src/room.ts:277-283) only verifies action.playerIdx === seatIdx; it special-cases advanceStep for turn order but not powerUp. The client wires the button at App.tsx:114 and enables it during your own Power-Up Step (packages/client/src/components/Board.tsx:207), i.e. exactly after the automatic power-up has already run.
findings.consequence: In the normal client flow the active player presses "Next Step" into the Power-Up Step (MP gains PUR, Allies gain 1), then presses the "Power Up" button and gains PUR again — and can keep pressing it. Since moveStage only clamps at the top of the ladder (turn.ts:96-98), an MP reaches its highest power stage every single turn regardless of PUR, which inflates its PAT rating, its damage, and its ability to absorb power-stage damage. Attrition, the core of the game, stops working.
findings.verifiedBy: CRD.txt L228-229 and the glossary line at L2551 ("Powering Up: This occurs during the Power Up Step of the Sequence of Play") match the quotes. reducer.ts:92 is `else if (state.step === 'powerUp') powerUp(state, state.activePlayerIdx, db, events);` — the full power-up applies on entering the step (engine.test.ts:72's own comment says "-> powerUp (auto power-up)"). reducer.ts:99-101 is `case 'powerUp': powerUp(state, action.playerIdx, db, events); break;` with no step check, no active-player check, and no once-per-turn flag anywhere in GameState (state.ts:202-228). turn.ts:132-140 powerUp() unconditionally moveStage(mp, PUR) and +1 per Ally; moveStage (turn.ts:99) only clamps with `Math.min(p.stageIndex + delta, ratings.length - 1)`. Server authorize() (packages/server/src/room.ts:277-283) checks only `named !== seatIdx` plus an advanceStep turn-order check — powerUp is not special-cased. Board.tsx:207 enables the button on `state.step !== 'powerUp'` being false, i.e. precisely after the automatic power-up ran. Grep of every *.test.ts finds no test asserting a once-per-turn power-up limit.

findings.title: The Declare Step is not a decision — the attacker is forced into Combat every turn
findings.crdEvidence: CRD.txt L211: "If you are the Attacker, you go through all 5 steps of a turn and can choose whether or not to declare Combat." L232-233: "4) Declare Step: In this ste you declare if you are going to enter Combat with your opponent. If you choose not to declare Combat skip the Combat Step and go to the Discard Step."
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/turn.ts:56-66 and packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:90-93
findings.defect: advanceStep unconditionally sets step to the next entry in STEPS, so 'declare' always becomes 'combat', and reducer.ts:93 then calls beginCombat(). The only escape is state.skipCombatThisTurn (turn.ts:57-63), which is set in exactly one place — noncombat.ts:82-85, when a Location or Battleground is played. There is no 'declareCombat' action in the Action union (a grep for 'declare' as a step turns up nothing outside the STEPS array), and the client's only step control is a blanket advanceStep button (packages/client/src/App.tsx:113, Board.tsx:204). The attacker has no way to say no.
findings.consequence: Every turn, the defender is handed 3 free cards by the forced Prepare Phase (combat.ts:79 draw(state, defender, PREPARE_DRAW)) and a full set of alternating Attack Phases, even when the attacker is empty-handed, out of power stages, or would rather fortify. Declining Combat to deny the opponent their draw and their attacks is a real strategic line in this game and it is unavailable. It also makes the Rejuvenation Step's condition ("you did not declare Combat") unreachable through play, and makes cards worded around the Declare Step inexpressible.
findings.verifiedBy: CRD.txt L211 and L232-233 read as quoted ("If you choose not to declare Combat skip the Combat Step and go to the Discard Step"). turn.ts:47-48 computes `const next: Step = STEPS[(i + 1) % STEPS.length]!` and turn.ts:64 sets `state.step = next` unconditionally, so 'declare' always becomes 'combat'; reducer.ts:93 then fires `beginCombat(state, db, events)`. The only bypass is turn.ts:58 `if (next === 'combat' && state.skipCombatThisTurn)`, and grep confirms skipCombatThisTurn is written in exactly one place, noncombat.ts:83, when a Location/Battleground is played. The Action union in packages/shared/src/protocol.ts:9-31 contains no 'declareCombat' or 'skipCombat' member — the only turn control is `{ type: 'advanceStep' }` (protocol.ts:13), wired to a single blanket button at App.tsx:113 / Board.tsx:204 ("Advance step"). The attacker has no representable way to decline Combat.

findings.title: Step-10 damage modifiers from Drills and cards in play are never applied
findings.crdEvidence: CRD L346 (Battle Sequence step 10): "Add and/or subtract any modifiers, from the attack, Drills, personality powers, etc., to the Base Damage." CRD L1371: Black Bear Hug Drill — "All of your physical attacks do +2 power stages of damage." CRD L1425: Blue Breakfall Drill — "All physical attacks performed against you do 2 less power stages of damage, to a minimum of 0."
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:677, packages/engine/src/drills.ts:1-49
findings.defect: The damage total is `const total = (atk.baseDamage ?? 0) + (atk.modifiers ?? 0) + (atk.ifSuccessfulStages ?? 0)`. `atk.modifiers` is only ever written by setupAttackAbility (abilities.ts:113) from the *attack card's own* parsed ability. No code path in combat.ts reads either player's `zones.inPlay` for damage modification — combat.ts touches inPlay only in activateDefenseShields (line 388) and findCombatCard (line 439). drills.ts implements only identification, style legality, and level-change discarding; it contains no damage logic at all.
findings.consequence: Every damage-modifying Drill is inert. A player with Black Bear Hug Drill and Black Striking Drill in play (+2 and +2 power stages to all physical attacks) deals PAT damage flat, and a defender with Blue Breakfall Drill or Black Physical Drill in play takes full PAT damage instead of the reduced amount. Since the shipped PAT (data/pat.json) yields 1 power stage for equal brackets, these Drills are usually the largest term in a physical attack's damage, so physical-damage totals are wrong in most normal games where either player runs Drills.
findings.verifiedBy: combat.ts:677 is verbatim `const total = (atk.baseDamage ?? 0) + (atk.modifiers ?? 0) + (atk.ifSuccessfulStages ?? 0);` — no term sourced from either player's board. `atk.modifiers` is written only at abilities.ts:113 `else attack.modifiers += e.stages;` inside setupAttackAbility, i.e. from the attack card itself. drills.ts (all 49 lines read) contains only isDrill, isFreestyleDrill and discardDrills — no damage logic. grep for `constant` across packages/engine/src non-test files returns nothing, so no continuous ability is ever executed; mastery.ts likewise states per-card Mastery powers are not modelled. CRD L1371 and L1425 read exactly as quoted. Minor slip: the auditor says combat.ts touches inPlay only at 388 and 439; it also does at 440 and 492 — but both are card lookup/placement, not damage, so the defect stands.

findings.title: The energy attack's 2-power-stage cost is not enforced — a personality at 0 stages attacks for free
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:397 "A cost exists on a card only if the word 'cost'... appears on the card itself. Energy attacks that don't tell you the basic cost on the card gain 'Costs 2 power stages to perform'." CRD:452 "Energy attacks that don't have their cost listed always cost 2 power stages." CRD:806 "Costs are compulsory actions required to play a card in the first place." CRD:390 "When a card effect causes you to lose power stages, not to a minimum of 0, if you go below 0, you must discard the top card of your life deck for every power stage left over."
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:257-262 (the return value of `loseStages` is discarded); packages/engine/src/combat.ts:99-108 (`loseStages` takes `Math.min(n, from)` and RETURNS the unpayable remainder)
findings.defect: declareAttack calls `loseStages(attCtl, ability?.cost?.powerStages ?? ENERGY_STAGE_COST, db, events)` and throws away the returned remainder. There is no affordability check before the attack is created, and the unpaid stages are neither refused nor converted to life-card discards. The damage path at combat.ts:529 does consume the remainder; both cost sites (combat.ts:259 and :261) drop it.
findings.consequence: A personality sitting at 0 power stages — which is exactly where MPs live once an Ally has taken over, CRD:583 — performs energy attacks at zero cost, every Attack Phase, indefinitely. A personality at 1 stage pays 1 instead of 2. The cost that is supposed to be the limiter on energy combat is effectively optional for the players who use energy attacks most.
findings.verifiedBy: combat.ts:258-259 `if (kind === 'energy') { loseStages(attCtl, ability?.cost?.powerStages ?? ENERGY_STAGE_COST, db, events); }` — the return value is discarded, and there is no affordability guard anywhere earlier in declareAttack (lines 221-233 check combat state, phase, lockouts and the card only). loseStages (combat.ts:99-108) does `const taken = Math.min(n, from); ... return n - taken;`, so an attacker at stageIndex 0 pays nothing and the unpayable remainder vanishes. Contrast combat.ts:529 `const overflow = loseStages(target, dmg, db, events);` which does consume it. CRD:397/452/806 are verbatim as quoted. One inaccuracy that does not change the defect: line 261 (`else if (ability?.cost?.powerStages)`) also drops the remainder, so the claim's 'only call site that drops it' is imprecise — both are cost sites of the same bug.

findings.title: Control of Combat does not return to the MP at the end of Combat
findings.crdEvidence: CRD L604: "The control of Combat always returns to the MP at the end of Combat." (distinct from L589, which governs control DURING combat)
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:168-175 (endCombatStep) and packages/engine/src/turn.ts:119-130 (releaseControlIfMpRecovered, MP_DOWN_STAGES)
findings.defect: endCombatStep's only release path is releaseControlIfMpRecovered, which returns false immediately unless `p.mp.stageIndex > MP_DOWN_STAGES` (turn.ts:121). An Ally only ever takes control while the MP is at stage 0 or 1 (combat.ts:911), which is exactly the case that check refuses to release, so the Ally keeps `inControlOfCombat` past the end of Combat. The same conditional guard is the only release on the new-turn path (turn.ts:55) and the Power-Up path (turn.ts:138), and with a typical PUR of 1 an MP at stage 0 powers up to stage 1 and is still "down", so control is never handed back. Nothing else clears the flag except an explicit player choice (combat.ts:339-345, 904, 912). The test suite encodes the wrong behaviour: control-of-combat.test.ts:100-106 asserts control is NOT released while the MP is down, and no test covers end of Combat.
findings.consequence: An Ally that took over in turn 1 is still in Control of Combat at the start of every later Combat Step. The attacking player's attacks are automatically performed by that Ally — declareAttack reads controllerOf() at combat.ts:237 — so the Physical Attack Table uses the Ally's power rating instead of the MP's without the player ever choosing, and the MP is treated as a redirect target (combat.ts:509-512) rather than the fighter.
findings.verifiedBy: CRD L604 reads exactly "The control of Combat always returns to the MP at the end of Combat." — unconditional, and distinct from L589's during-combat rule. combat.ts:168 `function endCombatStep` has one release path, `for (const p of state.players) releaseControlIfMpRecovered(state, p.idx);`, and turn.ts:119-121 opens with `if (!p || p.mp.stageIndex <= MP_DOWN_STAGES) return false;` with `MP_DOWN_STAGES = 1` at turn.ts:130. An Ally can only have taken control while the MP was at stage 0-1 (combat.ts:911 `if (player.mp.stageIndex > MP_DOWN_STAGES) return 'MP must be at its bottom 2 power stages';`), i.e. precisely the state the release refuses. The same guard is the only release on the new-turn path (turn.ts:55) and the Power-Up path (turn.ts:138). Nothing else clears inControlOfCombat except explicit player choice (combat.ts:339-345, 904, 912). All six tests in control-of-combat.test.ts were read: none touches endCombatStep or end-of-Combat, and the test at line 100 asserts `releaseControlIfMpRecovered(s, 0) === false` with the Ally retaining control. Downstream: declareAttack reads `controllerOf(state.players[attackerIdx]!)` at combat.ts:237 and redirectTargets (combat.ts:509-511) filters out only the controller, leaving the MP as a damage sink.

findings.title: Physical Base Damage is read from the PAT at declaration, before the defender names Control of Combat
findings.crdEvidence: CRD L328 (Battle Sequence step 4): "If an Ally can take over Combat for the Main Personality, the Defender must announce which personality is in Control of Combat until this attack is resolved." CRD L343 (step 9): "Determine the Base Damage ... by consulting the Physical Attack Table" — step 9 comes AFTER step 4. CRD L583: "You also use the Ally's power rating when the Physical Attack Table is used." CRD L576: "If your opponent has to use the Physical Attack Table, he still uses the power rating of the personality in control of Combat."
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:238 and :265-266 (baseDamage computed in declareAttack from `defCtl.currentRating`); packages/engine/src/combat.ts:325-350 (resolveControlOfCombat updates `atk.defenderControllerUid` at :347 but never recomputes `atk.baseDamage`); packages/engine/src/pat.ts:96-104
findings.defect: declareAttack captures `defCtl = controllerOf(defender)` at line 238 and immediately calls `computeBaseDamage(attCtl.currentRating, defCtl.currentRating)` at line 266 — i.e. at battle-sequence step 1/2. Only afterwards does openControlWindow (line 276) ask the defender who is in Control of Combat. resolveControlOfCombat re-reads the controller into `defenderControllerUid` (line 347) so the damage lands on the newly named personality, but `atk.baseDamage` is never recalculated, and `computeBaseDamage` (pat.ts:96-104) is a function of the DEFENDER's rating bracket. The engine runs step 9 during step 1.
findings.consequence: An Ally may only take over while the MP is at its bottom 2 power stages, so the MP's rating is at or near the bottom of its ladder and the attacker's PAT bracket advantage is at its maximum. The defender switches control to a healthy Ally, the log and UI show the Ally in control and taking the hit, but the damage dealt is still the number computed against the crippled MP. Concretely: MP at stage 1 (rating 100, bracket A) with an Ally at stage 3 (rating 300, bracket B) — with the placeholder table an attacker in bracket B deals 2 instead of 1, and with a real PAT the swing is larger. The Ally loses more power stages than the PAT allows, and the excess overflows into extra life cards — which can also push the attack over the 5-life-card Dragon Ball capture threshold it should not have reached.
findings.verifiedBy: combat.ts:238 `const defCtl = controllerOf(state.players[defenderIdx]!);` then combat.ts:266 `attack.baseDamage = computeBaseDamage(attCtl.currentRating, defCtl.currentRating);` — this runs before combat.ts:276 `if (openControlWindow(state, attack, db)) return undefined;`. pat.ts:96-104 `const di = bracketOf(defender, table); return table.damage[ai]?.[di] ?? 0;` makes it a function of the defender's rating. In resolveControlOfCombat the only write is combat.ts:347 `atk.defenderControllerUid = controllerOf(defender).uid;` with the comment "Control decides who the damage lands on, so re-read it now" — the rating is not re-read. grep confirms computeBaseDamage has exactly one call site (combat.ts:266), so the stale value is what reaches combat.ts:677 `const total = (atk.baseDamage ?? 0) + ...` and applyPowerStageDamage (combat.ts:515-528), which reads `atk.pendingPowerStageDamage` with no recompute. CRD L328, L343, L576 and L583 are verbatim as quoted. The engine's own test at battle-sequence.test.ts:133-145 ('naming the Ally makes it the one that takes the damage', MP stage 1 / Ally stage 3) asserts only defenderControllerUid and that the Ally's stage dropped, so the stale rating passes unnoticed; control-of-combat.test.ts covers who holds control and when it releases, never the PAT number after a switch.

findings.title: Damage-prevention cards resolve as a complete stop of the attack instead of reducing damage
findings.crdEvidence: CRD L446: "Preventing damage from the attack is not counted as modifying damage from the attack." CRD L305-306 lists stopping and preventing as distinct defensive effects ("...that stops an attack or prevents damage from an attack"). findings.title: A combat-long stop bars the attacker from declaring rather than stopping the attack after it is performed

findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:228-229 in declareAttack (lockoutAgainst at combat.ts:185-194)
findings.defect: declareAttack returns the error string "<type> attacks are stopped for the remainder of this Combat" before any of the attack is performed — before costs at combat.ts:258-262, before setupAttackAbility's secondary effects at combat.ts:255, and before the card is spent at combat.ts:652/632. The CRD models these floating effects as stops applied to a performed attack (step 7/8 of the Battle Sequence), which is why Orange Energy Discharge can be printed as an exception to them and why "if this attack is stopped" riders exist.

findings.title: Battle-sequence steps 14 and 15 run in the wrong order: "If successful" effects resolve before the Dragon Ball capture is offered
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:358 "14) If the attack does 5 or more life cards of damage, the attacker may capture an opponent's Dragon Ball." CRD:361 "15) Any 'If successful' effects that the attacker has are resolved."
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:750 (`finishSuccessfulAttack` — which sets `resolutionStep = 15` at combat.ts:152 and runs `applyIfSuccessful`) is called before packages/engine/src/combat.ts:759-770 (`capturableBalls` and the step-14 capture prompt)
findings.defect: In resolveLifeCardDamage the if-successful chain is resolved at line 750, and only afterwards is the set of capturable Dragon Balls read (line 759) and the capture prompt raised (line 761). `atk.resolutionStep` is therefore never 14 — it jumps 13 -> 15 — so the sequence display reports 15 while the engine still owes step 14, and the capture happens in a step the display says has already passed.
findings.consequence: The set of capturable balls is evaluated against post-step-15 state. An "If successful" effect that changes which Dragon Balls are in play — removing one from the defender's control, or one that ends the game — resolves before the attacker is offered the capture that 5+ life cards of damage earned them, so a capture the CRD grants can be silently withdrawn; and any if-successful effect the attacker would rather order after seeing the capture result is forced to resolve first. In the common case where the if-successful chain touches only anger, stages or cards, the outcome is unchanged.

Caveat on the stated consequence: no Effect kind can currently move or protect a Dragon Ball (the union at shared/abilities.ts:23-63 has no such kind), so today the harm is the ordering/step-display inversion and the forced resolution order, not an emptied capture list — which is why this is scoped as an edge case.
